eyebrow: AI Engineering Leadership & Architecture · Chapter Two
subtitle: Lesson 8 · Architecture Decision-Making

eyebrow: When no option wins on every axis
code:
Option A: cheapest, middling latency & quality
Option B: best latency & quality, costs more
Option C: balanced, excels at nothing

"Which is best" has no single honest answer.
caption: The real question: best for what we care about, weighted the way we actually care about it.

code:
weights = cost .35, latency .25,
          quality .25, maintainability .15

Option A: weighted score = 7.10
Option B: weighted score = 6.90
Option C: weighted score = 7.00
caption: Score each option 1-10 per criterion; weights reflect relative importance and sum to 1.0.

eyebrow: The real decision is the weights
code:
Scoring (how good at cost, at latency) is
the easy, relatively objective part.

Weights (how much we care about cost vs.
latency vs. maintainability) are where the
actual judgment call lives.
caption: Two engineers can agree on every score and still recommend different options -- because they weighted differently.

eyebrow: Run a sensitivity check before trusting a close result
code:
A: 7.10  vs.  C: 7.00  -- genuinely close

How much would the weights have to shift
before the ranking flips?

Close result = worth a real conversation.
Robust result = more solid than it feels.
caption: A close score is itself an honest, important result -- not a landslide any reasonable weighting would reach.
